deliverables.text: Model-and-derivative worksheet for the current wave: check the fitted cubic against the reported series at three weeks; differentiate term by term with the power rule; state the derivative at the decision week with units as an instantaneous rate of change and separate it from the average rate of change over the last two reported weeks; close with a note on why the reported series is not differentiable at its own data points.

Tangent-line projection: the equation of the tangent to the current-wave model at the decision week, drawn with the model and the reported points, and the week that straight line reaches the board's written level versus the week the curve itself reaches it.

Critical-point table for the previous wave: every critical point of that fitted model inside its window, each classified by the first derivative test as a local maximum or local minimum, with its calendar week and its meaning on the ground, plus an explicit note on any critical point whose fitted value could not be a real case count.

Concavity sign chart for the current wave: the second derivative, the week its sign changes, that week marked on the graph, and a plain-English statement of what 'the curve turned in that week' means and why it is the earliest defensible warning available.

Retrospective optimisation on the previous wave: the start week for a closure of the board's authorised length that would have covered the most reported cases, i.e. maximise G(w) = P(w) + P(w+1) -- objective function, its derivative, the critical point, and a first-derivative-test confirmation that it is a maximum -- reported as a distance in weeks from that wave's concavity turn, plus whether that wave ever crossed the board's written level at all.

The decision table: chain-weighted in-school transmissions per one thousand students left over the horizon under each plan, built from the stated formula, with the model's rate of change at the first and last week of each closure window used to explain the size of the gap between the two plans, ending in a recommendation.

balance.argument_a: Under the fitted model The Early Brake leaves 32.5844 chain-weighted in-school transmissions per 1,000 students against The Tripwire's 36.8926, out of a no-action total of 62.8646 -- a margin of 11.68%. It spends the closure budget on horizon weeks 12 and 13, whose chain multipliers (7.8744 and 6.2039) are the two largest available, while The Tripwire spends it two weeks later on multipliers of 4.6964 and 3.3359. It also depends on no assumed testing programme.
balance.argument_b: The Tripwire removes 10% of in-school transmission in every open week of the horizon for zero instructional days, and keeps an irreversible once-per-term budget in reserve. Appendix A settles the rest on its own: the previous wave peaked at a fitted 302.67 cases against a board level of 818.87 cases, so a district on The Tripwire would have spent nothing at all that autumn and still held its budget. Its 36.8926 is 11.68% behind, not a different order of magnitude.
balance.margin_basis: Chain-weighted in-school transmissions per one thousand students remaining over the horizon, computed for each plan from Appendix D's fully stated formula once the real series, the population denominator, the board's level, the horizon, k and the programme effectiveness land. Margin = (worse - better) / worse.
balance.twist_effect: Replacing the model's forecast with the county's real reported counts for the six horizon weeks -- and crediting each prevented transmission with the chain the county actually went on to have rather than the planning growth rate -- flips the verdict. The Early Brake leaves 67.9992, The Tripwire 61.1993, a 10.00% margin the other way. The board's level is crossed in week 12 rather than week 14, so the whole earliest-warning advantage disappears: both plans close in the same week and the only difference left is the screening programme.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Birchmont Unified School District, Dr. Renata Vance, the board and its standing rules
modeling_assumptions.basis: The county, the weekly series (S1) and the population denominator (S2/S3) are real and cited. The district, the officer and the decision are not. Background says so in the open rather than implying a real body made this call.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Not numeric. Governs how every other row reads: real data, invented governance.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: The board's own written closure level (the Tripwire's trigger)
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public threshold exists for a fictional district. CDC's national four-level scale (S4) tops out at '100 or more' per 100,000 per 7 days, and Chittenden County sat above that top tier in every week of Appendix B, so an escalation trigger has to be set above the top of the national scale. 500 is five times the CDC high-transmission floor and sits between the two plans' computed closure weeks rather than on top of either. Real school-closure thresholds are not a single universal number either -- CDC's own 2020 school-decision framework (see case.md Background and Appendix G) publishes several risk-tiered ranges at once and leaves the actual operating-status call to local officials, which is the same reason this board's own written level has to be stated here as a scenario assumption rather than looked up.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The most consequential number in the case, and deliberately NOT swept in Tier 2 probe 5: halving a plan's own written trigger produces a different Option B, not a sensitivity test of an estimate. Swept and disclosed anyway (case.json.derived.disclosed_threshold_sweep, QA_REPORT.md): at 250 the Tripwire fires in the same week as the Early Brake and B wins by exactly the screening removal rate (10.00%); at 750 the forecast never reaches it inside the horizon, the Tripwire never fires, and A wins by 42.41% -- outside the SPEC section 2 cap. Both disclosed, neither hidden.

modeling_assumptions.value_used: two weeks (ten instructional days), once per term
modeling_assumptions.basis: Board constraints of this shape were real, but no public document fixes a number for a fictional district. Fixing it makes both plans cost the same, which is what lets the primary metric compare what the budget buys rather than what it costs.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Not swept: a three-week or one-week budget is a different board rule, not a different estimate. It cancels out of the comparison while both plans spend the same budget.

modeling_assumptions.value_used: the six weeks after the decision week (t = 12 through t = 17)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Long enough for the chain multiplier to differ meaningfully across the horizon, short enough that a board would actually score it.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Not swept, same reason as MA3. A longer horizon raises every chain multiplier and widens the gap; a shorter one narrows it.

modeling_assumptions.basis: The real district calendar has a winter break inside this horizon and the case ignores it. A stated simplification, not an oversight.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Does not enter the primary metric at all -- both plans spend the same closure budget, so instructional days never appear in the arithmetic. It would matter immediately if the metric charged days, and a Hero who raises it has found a real edge of the model.

modeling_assumptions.value_used: 0.5 in-school transmissions per 1,000 students in an open week at a community rate of 100 per 100,000 that week
modeling_assumptions.basis: Reasoned down from S6: at 100 reported cases per 100,000 per week, roughly one reported case per 1,000 students per week; roughly twenty in-school close contacts per case; school-associated secondary attack rates of 0.7%-2% in mitigated K-12 settings; and reported cases undercounting infections. Those bracket roughly 0.3-0.8 and 0.5 sits inside.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Cancels out of the comparison entirely -- both plans scale linearly in k. Flexed +/-50% in Tier 2 probe 5 the winner and the margin do not move at all (11.68% at 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75). It sets the size of the numbers, not the answer.

modeling_assumptions.value_used: 0.10 of in-school transmission removed per open week
modeling_assumptions.basis: Built down from S5: 55.0% average sensitivity in asymptomatic people is the ceiling, and a real programme loses further ground to partial consent, a twice-weekly cadence against an infectious period shorter than the gap between tests, and time-to-result. 0.10 is a deliberately conservative programme-level figure, not the test's sensitivity.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The largest genuinely-estimated lever. Flexed +/-50% in Tier 2 probe 5 (0.05 to 0.15): the winner does not change and the margin ranges 6.48%-16.33%.

modeling_assumptions.value_used: a prevented transmission is credited with the geometric chain it would have started, at the planning growth rate g, truncated at the horizon
modeling_assumptions.basis: A modelling choice, not a measurement. It asserts that onward spread compounds at the same relative rate the fitted curve is growing at on the decision week, and that the credit stops at the horizon. It is the entire quantitative reason early action can beat late action, and it is asserted, not proven.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Flexed +/-50% on g in Tier 2 probe 5: the winner does not change and the margin ranges 7.76%-15.61%. A Hero who argues the chain should be credited at a falling rate once a wave peaks has made a real argument this case cannot refute -- and the twist shows exactly what happens when it is.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Timing convention -- when the Tripwire's closure starts once its level is crossed
modeling_assumptions.value_used: the closure covers week tB itself and tB+1; no reporting or decision lag
modeling_assumptions.basis: Appendix D, Step 5 writes this out as X(tB) + X(tB+1), and both plans are scored the same way: the Early Brake's window is the first two horizon weeks, the Tripwire's is the first two weeks from its crossing. It is the reading most generous to the Tripwire, because a level read off reported data cannot in reality be acted on until the week it describes has finished. It is a choice, not a measurement, and is stated in Appendix F because of that.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Load-bearing: the stated margin holds only under it. Push the Tripwire's window one week later -- by a one-week reporting lag, or by reading the crossing week off D2's tangent line (t = 14.4171) instead of off the curve (t = 13.7293) -- and it closes weeks 15 and 16, leaving 41.5402 and losing by 21.56%, past the 20% balance cap. Under the twist's real reported counts the same one-week lag has the Tripwire leave 68.4202 against the Early Brake's 67.9992, a 0.62% margin the other way, and the twist's reversal disappears.

sensitivity_note: SPEC §6 applies. This case is built on a real respiratory-illness wave and on a school-closure decision; some Heroes in the room will have lost school time, or people, to one. The framing is deliberately administrative and protective — transmissions prevented and instructional days spent, never deaths optimised — and no learner is asked to price a life. Flag the topic before the launch and give anyone who wants it a way out of the room.
